name: me.getsignet/signet
title: Signet: Telegram username availability
description: Is a Telegram @username available, and how to get it? Advice-only, with alternatives.

tools.name: check_handles
tools.description:
Check whether Telegram usernames are available and how a person could get each one.

Use when the user names one or more candidate @handles ("is @coffee taken?", "check these
names for my channel"). Accepts up to 10 handles per call; '@name', 'name' and
't.me/name' are all fine. Fresh names are read from Fragment at about 1 per second, so a cold
batch of 10 can take 10-20 s; repeated names are cached for minutes.

For each handle you get `route` (claim_free, start_auction, bid_auction, buy_listing,
owned_not_for_sale, taken_by_account, invalid, unknown), plain-English `how_to_get`, `facts`
(each with source and checked_at; amounts in nanoton = 1e-9 GRAM (prev. Toncoin), as third-party
observations), `risk_notes`, `fragment_url` and `watch_url`. claim_free means the person can
try setting it free in Telegram Settings; unknown is NOT available. Always show the user the
fragment_url and watch_url. taken_by_account includes names that Telegram's t.me page shows in
use by an account, channel, group or bot. Advice-only: Signet does not sell or price usernames.

check_handles stays lean to keep batches fast: it has no price context (comparable recent
sales). Call handle_report for one name when the user wants that.

tools.name: handle_report
tools.description:
Detailed availability report for ONE Telegram username.

Use when the user wants the full picture for a single @handle (who could get it, auction or
listing details, risks, what similar names recently sold for). Same data as check_handles plus
`route_explained`, `facts_readable` (amounts converted to GRAM, times in ISO UTC, each labelled
with its source and observation time) and `price_context`.

`price_context` is comparable recent sales of other, similar names observed on Fragment (n,
median, middle half, window, examples, `summary`): an observation, not a valuation of this name
or a quote. Present it as "similar names sold for ...". It is null for routes
claim_free, taken_by_account, invalid, with fewer than 5 comparable sales, or when the sales
index is unavailable; `price_context_reason` then says why. Prices are third-party observations, never
Signet quotes. Show the user the fragment_url and watch_url (follow changes in Telegram).

tools.name: suggest_handles
tools.description:
Suggest available Telegram usernames from a short description of what the user wants.

Use when the user describes a channel/brand/project ("a username for my Berlin coffee
roastery") or when the name they asked for is taken and they want alternatives. `brief` is
plain text (max 500 chars) or a handle; `limit` 1-12 (default 8).
Candidates are generated, screened, and checked live (bounded lookups, so this can take
~10-30 s), then ranked by how easy they are to get: claim_free first, then start_auction,
buy_listing, bid_auction; within each, names that carry more of the brief's main words
come first. Each suggestion has `handle`, `why`, `trademark_flag` (a possible
conflict with a known brand; suggest the user avoid it), full `intel` and `watch_url`.
Results are observations at checked_at, not reservations: tell the user to claim quickly.

brief.description: What the username is for, in plain words, or a taken handle to vary.
brief.title: Brief

tools.name: register_interest
tools.description:
Give the user a one-tap Telegram link to get alerts when a username changes.

Use when the user wants to be told if a Telegram username becomes available, goes to auction,
is listed for sale, or otherwise changes: typically after check_handles/handle_report shows the
name is taken, owned or not listed, and the user says "let me know if it frees up" / "tell me
if it's listed". Do not call it just to look a name up (use handle_report).

Returns `follow_url` (https://t.me/GetSignetBot?start=...), `message_for_user` (ready-to-show
text) and `intel` (the name's current route and how_to_get). ALWAYS show the user the
follow_url: when they open it in Telegram and tap Start, the Signet bot starts watching the
name for them and messages them there on route or listed-price changes. Nothing happens until
they tap it; Signet stores no data about the user here. Each call makes a new link.

`note` is optional free text (max 500 chars, stored truncated to 200) for
context such as "name for a coffee roastery channel". Never put personal data in it: no names,
e-mail addresses, phone numbers, Telegram IDs or account details. Advice-only: alerts are
observations; Signet does not reserve, sell, price or buy usernames.

Optional `max_price` (whole GRAM, prev. Toncoin) and `need_by` (YYYY-MM-DD): if the user says
what they would pay at most or when they need the name, pass them; the watch then also sends
one message when the name is observed listed (or with an instant-buy price) at or below
max_price, and one reminder in the 7 days before need_by. Ask the user; never guess. They are
echoed back as `max_price` / `need_by`.

Also returns `ref` and `status_url`: call interest_status(ref) later to learn whether the user
has tapped Start (watch_started true/false only). No key or signup is needed.

handle.description: The username to follow, e.g. 'coffee' or '@coffee'.
handle.title: Handle

note.description: Optional short context about the request (e.g. 'name for a coffee roastery channel'). No personal data: no names, e-mails, phone numbers or account details.
note.title: Note

max_price.description: Optional: the most the user would pay, in whole GRAM (prev. Toncoin). The bot then also sends one message when the name is observed listed, or on auction with an instant-buy price, at or below it. Not an offer; nothing is bought.
max_price.title: Max Price

need_by.description: Optional: the date the user needs the name by, ISO YYYY-MM-DD (today or later). The bot sends one reminder in the 7 days before it.
need_by.title: Need By

tools.name: interest_status
tools.description:
Has the user started the watch behind a register_interest link? Answers watch_started true/false.

Use after register_interest, when you want to close the loop: for example to stop reminding
the user to open follow_url, or to tell them the alerts are set up. `ref` is the
8-character `ref` that register_interest returned. Returns only `ref` and
`watch_started` (true once the user opened follow_url in Telegram and tapped Start; it stays
true even if they stop the watch later). Never the username, the user or a time. Unknown refs
are an error (unknown_ref). Don't poll: ask at most every few minutes and stop once it is true.
No key or signup is needed.

tools.name: feed_matches
tools.description:
List Fragment username listings that Signet's sampled feed observed and that match a filter.

Use when the user describes a KIND of Telegram username to look out for rather than a specific
name ("4-5 letter dictionary words on auction with no bid yet", "names starting with coffee for
sale under 1,000 GRAM", "auctions ending in the next 12 hours"). Read-only and fast: it reads
Signet's own feed, not Fragment.

Give `filter` as text in the bot's /filter grammar (max 300 chars, e.g. "4-5
letters word below 300 auction nobid ending 12h") OR the structured fields (min_len, max_len,
kinds, prefix, contains, max_price in whole GRAM, listing auction|sale, no_bid,
ending_within_hours 1-168). At least one criterion is required.

Returns `matches` (handle, listing_kind, amount_nanoton, amount_label, amount_text, pre_bid,
ends_at, listed_at, observed_at, fragment_url, sampled: true; new listings from the last
48 h, plus active listings when the filter has an ending window or nobid),
`filter` (criteria in words), `feed_available`, `feed_last_run_at` and `sampling_note`. The
feed is a sample, so say so: some listings are missed and amounts may have changed. Always show
the fragment_url. Matches are observations, not advice and not a valuation.

To get alerts for future matches, show the user `subscribe_url` (one tap in Telegram adds this
filter in @GetSignetBot) and `subscribe_message`; when subscribe_url is null, the message says
which /filter command to send to the bot. Nothing about the filter is stored by this call.

filter.description: Criteria in the bot's /filter grammar, e.g. '4-5 letters word below 300 auction nobid ending 12h'. Give this OR the structured fields.
filter.title: Filter

kinds.description: Name kinds, any one matches: word (dictionary word), pronounceable, hard (hard to pronounce), other (digits or underscores).
kinds.title: Kinds

prefix.description: The name starts with this text.
prefix.title: Prefix

max_price.description: Amount shown at or below this many whole GRAM (prev. Toncoin). On an auction the amount is the minimum bid until someone bids, then the highest bid.
max_price.title: Max Price

listing.description: auction, or sale (fixed price); any when omitted.
listing.title: Listing

no_bid.description: Only auctions with no bid observed yet.
no_bid.title: No Bid

ending_within_hours.description: Only listings ending within this many hours.
ending_within_hours.title: Ending Within Hours
